name: Saint Joseph the Worker
history: Pius XII instituted this feast in 1955 to give May Day, the festival of labour, a Christian meaning. Jesus was known in Nazareth as the carpenter’s son, and Joseph shows the dignity of ordinary work done honestly for family and neighbour. The day is a reminder of the Church’s teaching on the rights of workers.
life: The Gospels call Joseph a tekton, a craftsman, and Jesus Himself was known as ‘the carpenter’. For some thirty years the Son of God lived a hidden life of work in a small town, learning a trade from His foster father. The Church has always seen in this a sign that work is not a curse but a share in God’s own creating. In 1891 Leo XIII, in Rerum Novarum, defended the right of workers to a just wage and to form associations, and later popes developed his teaching. When Pius XII addressed Italian workers on 1 May 1955 he gave them this feast, so that the day already kept by working people around the world would also honour the patron of workers. John Paul II, who had himself worked in a quarry and a factory, wrote in Laborem Exercens that through work man becomes more a man.
prayerTo: Saint Joseph the Worker, you earned your bread by the work of your hands and taught the Son of God your trade. Pray for all who work and all who cannot find work, for employers and those they employ. Help me to do my work well, honestly and for the glory of God. Amen.
penance: Do your ordinary work today with special care, offering it to God. Thank someone whose work serves you, and pray for those who are unemployed or underpaid.
meditation: Is not this the carpenter? The townspeople meant it as a dismissal. How might your own ordinary work become a place of holiness?
prayer: O God, Creator of all things, Who dost impose on man the law of work; grant in Thy goodness that, by the example and patronage of blessed Joseph, we may both accomplish the work Thou dost command and attain the reward Thou hast promised. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
